learning_outcomes.text: Has knowledge regarding the architecture of AVR family microcontrollers.
Has knowledge about the operation and control of peripheral devices (general-purpose input/output ports, A/D, D/A converters, counters/timers) available in AVR microcontrollers.
Has knowledge about the operation of basic serial communication interfaces in AVR microcontrollers: USART, I2C (TWI), SPI.
Knows the technique of connecting external devices to a microcontroller and the basics of designing input and output interfaces.
Knows basic techniques of software handling for serial communication interfaces.
Knows basic ways to use built-in peripheral devices for measuring basic quantities (voltage, period (frequency), duty cycle, etc.).
Has knowledge regarding the organization of 8-bit microcontroller software and methods for testing and commissioning it.
Is able to programmatically control microcontroller peripheral devices (I/O ports, counters/timers, A/D and D/A converters).
Is able to design simple hardware interfaces for handling selected digital and analog input and output signals.
Is able to design software for the microcontroller to support basic devices, and to commission and test it using integrated programming environments.
Is able to assess the suitability of a given microcontroller for solving a given task and develop simple input/output interfaces.
Is able to creatively use the capabilities of modern microcontrollers.
Is able to use materials and knowledge available on specialized internet portals.

syllabus_topics: Structure and basic parameters of AVR microcontrollers. Architecture of 8-bit AVR family microcontrollers. Electrical parameters of systems. Overview of available peripheral devices. Processor and memory map of microcontrollers based on AVR ATmega and ATxmega family systems.

Structure and operation of universal input/output ports. Structure of the universal input/output subsystem (PORT) exemplified by ATxmega microcontrollers. Programming the configuration of a pin as an output and/or input with required properties. Overview of registers for PORT subsystem operation. Examples of PORT subsystem operation in C language.

Interrupt system and event system in ATxmega microcontrollers. Interrupt sources, interrupt vector. Interrupt priorities. PMIC interrupt controller. Overview of registers for interrupt handling. Rules for writing interrupt service routines. EVSYS event system.

Structure and operation of analog peripherals (ADC, DAC, AC). Structure of A/D (ADC) and D/A (DAC) converters and analog comparator (AC) used in AVR ATxmega microcontrollers. Overview of registers for operation. Interrupts generated by these devices. Examples of software operation of ADC, DAC, and AC with and without using interrupts and/or event system.

Structure and operation of the counter/timer subsystem. Structure of the universal counter/timer subsystem used in ATxmega family microcontrollers. Clock signal sources for counters. Configuration of the counter/timer subsystem in comparison and capture modes. Interrupts from the timer subsystem.

Applications of the counter/timer subsystem in comparison mode. Use of counters/timers to generate pulses of a given duration and rectangular waveforms of a given frequency, duty cycle, and offset. Examples of counter/timer operation in comparison mode.

Applications of the counter/timer subsystem in capture mode. Use of counters/timers to measure pulse duration, period and duty cycle of a rectangular waveform, offset between two waveforms. Example of using counters/timers to measure parameters of rectangular waveforms.

Basic information about serial communication interfaces. Characteristics of USART, I2C (TWI) and SPI transmission standards. Structure of USART, TWI and SPI controllers in ATxmega family microcontrollers. Registers and software operation of individual interfaces. Use and handling of interrupts generated by USART, TWI and SPI controllers.

Structure and operation of the clock generator, power management, and reset subsystem. Structure of the clock signal generator and power management subsystem of ATxmega series microcontrollers. Distribution of the clock signal to individual blocks of the system. Microcontroller reset circuit. Software possibilities for reducing power consumption.

Flash and EEPROM memory subsystem. Organization of Flash program memory and non-volatile EEPROM memory in AVR microcontrollers. Configuration of Flash memory sections. Securing Flash memory content. EEPROM memory operation.
Overview of available AVR microcontrollers. Overview of universal AVR ATtiny, AVR ATmega, and AVR ATxmega family microcontrollers.
assessment_rules: For lectures, verification is via a test. For laboratory classes, verification is via execution of laboratory classes and a report. Credit for lectures depends on conditions specified in "Conditions and method of credit for individual forms of classes" and "Rules of participation in classes". Credit for laboratory classes depends on conditions specified in "Conditions and method of credit for individual forms of classes" and "Rules of participation in classes"; students must be prepared for the exercise, which may be verified by an oral or written colloquium. Passing the module is possible after passing all laboratory classes.
